author: sjm41
body:
@srengel 
S. cerevisiae LPL1 (S000005585, Q08448) is annotated to GO:0004622 lysophospholipase activity from PMID: 25014274.

We've just changed to the label of that GO term to the more specific 'phosphatidylcholine lysophospholipase activity' to match the definition and xrefs of the term - see https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30258

Looking at the paper and the 'has input' on the yeast annotation, I think the LPL1 annotation needs updating to the new term:
GO:0120559 phosphatidylethanolamine lysophospholipase activity

@marcfeuermann 
This affects https://www.pantree.org/node/annotationNode.jsp?id=PTN000280739
title: LPL1 (S000005585, Q08448) annotation to GO:0004622 lysophospholipase activity

author: marcfeuermann
body:
From PMID:25014274, LPL1 has indeed a broad substrate specificity. This is well annotated in UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot:
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q08448/entry
I think many reactions could be mapped (from Rhea) to LPL1 and propagated to closest orthologs via PAINT.
This ticket really requires more work ;-)

author: cmungall
body:
For LPL1, the gene review agents suggests the correct GO term is actually phospholipase B activity

https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/1fc95cca8dcb9cf90b6f39cae6b27168f6d1bec3/genes/yeast/LPL1/LPL1-ai-review.yaml#L47-L54 

```yaml
   proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0102545
      label: phospholipase B activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:25014274
      supporting_text: The purified Lpl1p showed phospholipase activity with broader
        substrate specificity, acting on all glycerophospholipids primarily at sn-2
        position and later at sn-1 position.
```

See discusson here:

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1xBFIQE0jt7K6kFg4zFzUwLDHtnDWat2ZVDarhcpA3_4/edit?slide=id.g38272bea041_0_11#slide=id.g38272bea041_0_11 (slides 30-38)

It suggests capturing the individual specificities as extensions
